title: Crisis Management & PR
completion_message: ¡Brillante! Las crisis definen a las empresas y a sus líderes. Manejar el vocabulario de relaciones públicas ('Damage control', 'Scapegoat', 'Backlash') te prepara para navegar y sobrevivir a las tormentas mediáticas más intensas del mundo corporativo.

stages.title: Gestión de Crisis y Relaciones Públicas (C2)

parts.visual:
1. Damage control (Control de daños): 
- Acciones tomadas para minimizar las consecuencias negativas de un incidente. 
Ej: After the scandal broke, the PR team went into damage control mode. 

2. Backlash (Reacción violenta / Represalia pública): 
- Una fuerte reacción negativa del público contra una decisión o evento. 
Ej: The company faced severe backlash over their new pricing policy. 

3. Scapegoat (Chivo expiatorio): 
- Persona o grupo al que se culpa por los errores de otros. 
Ej: The junior manager was used as a scapegoat to protect the CEO.
parts.audio: Welcome to Crisis Management and PR. Number 1: Damage control. These are actions taken to minimize the negative consequences of an incident. For example: After the scandal broke, the P R team went into damage control mode. Number 2: Backlash. A strong, negative public reaction against a decision or event. For example: The company faced severe backlash over their new pricing policy. Number 3: Scapegoat. A person or group made to bear the blame for others. For example: The junior manager was used as a scapegoat to protect the CEO.

parts.visual:
4. To sweep under the rug (Barrer bajo la alfombra / Ocultar): 
- Intentar esconder un problema o error en lugar de enfrentarlo. 
Ej: You can't just sweep a massive data breach under the rug! 

5. To blow over (Pasar / Olvidarse): 
- Cuando un escándalo o crisis pierde intensidad y se olvida. 
Ej: If we stay quiet, this scandal will eventually blow over. 

6. PR stunt (Truco publicitario): 
- Algo inusual hecho principalmente para atraer la atención de los medios. 
Ej: The CEO jumping out of a plane was just a PR stunt. 

7. Fall guy (Cabeza de turco / El que asume la culpa): 
- Similar a scapegoat, la persona que asume la culpa de un plan fallido.
parts.audio: Number 4: To sweep under the rug. This means to hide a problem or error instead of dealing with it. For example: You can't just sweep a massive data breach under the rug! Number 5: To blow over. When a scandal or crisis loses intensity and is forgotten. For example: If we stay quiet, this scandal will eventually blow over. Number 6: PR stunt. Something unusual done primarily to attract media attention. For example: The CEO jumping out of a plane was just a PR stunt. Number 7: Fall guy. Similar to a scapegoat, this is the person who takes the blame for a failed plan.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término correcto de gestión de crisis.

questions.question: As soon as the video leaked, our PR department went into full ____ control. (Control de daños).
The decision to fire 5,000 workers caused a massive public ____. (Reacción negativa/Rechazo).
The executives made the mistake, but the intern was used as a ____ to take the blame. (Chivo expiatorio).
You can't just sweep a million-dollar accounting error under the ____! (Barrer bajo la alfombra).
questions.explanation: Sweep under the rug = ocultar un problema.

questions.question: Don't issue a statement yet. Let's wait a few days and see if the scandal will ____ over. (Pasar / Olvidarse).
questions.explanation: Blow over = calmarse, pasar al olvido.

questions.question: The millionaire giving away cars on the street was clearly just a PR ____ to gain followers. (Truco publicitario).
questions.explanation: PR stunt = truco o maniobra publicitaria.

questions.question: When the illegal operation was discovered, the project manager became the ____ guy. (Cabeza de turco).
questions.explanation: Fall guy = el que asume la culpa, cabeza de turco.

questions.question: The company issued a public ____ to express their deep regret over the oil spill. (Disculpa).
The constant bad news caused severe damage to the brand's ____. (Reputación).
During a crisis, you must strictly follow the crisis ____ plan. (Gestión/Manejo).
questions.explanation: Crisis management plan = plan de gestión de crisis.

questions.question: We need to hire a spin ____ to change the media's narrative about our company. (Experto en relaciones públicas/manipulación mediática).
questions.explanation: Spin doctor = asesor de imagen/relaciones públicas especializado en dar un giro favorable a las noticias.

questions.question: The company's stock price took a ____ after the CEO was arrested. (Caída en picada).
questions.explanation: Take a nosedive = caer en picada.

questions.question: They tried to ____ the crisis by minimizing the number of affected users in the report. (Quitar importancia).
The incident was a total PR ____. It couldn't have gone worse. (Pesadilla/Desastre).
questions.explanation: PR nightmare = pesadilla de relaciones públicas.

questions.question: To regain public trust, we must be completely ____ about what went wrong. (Transparentes).
The press completely tore his reputation to ____. (Hizo trizas).
We are facing a media ____. Every news channel is talking about our failure. (Tormenta mediática).
The CEO had to step down amidst ____ of fraud and embezzlement. (Acusaciones).
The company is trying to ____ the flames of the scandal by firing the executives involved. (Apagar el fuego/Calmar).
questions.explanation: Douse the flames (o put out the fire) = apagar el escándalo. ('Fan the flames' sería empeorarlo).

questions.question: The scandal was a severe blow to the company's ____ line. (Beneficios netos/Rentabilidad final).
questions.explanation: Bottom line = el resultado financiero final (beneficio/pérdida).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra de crisis/PR correcta.

questions.question: ____ control. (Control de daños con D)
Public ____. (Reacción negativa/Rechazo con B)
He was the ____. (Chivo expiatorio con S)
He was the ____ guy. (Cabeza de turco con F)
Sweep under the ____. (Alfombra con R)
It will ____ over. (Pasar al olvido con B)
A PR ____. (Truco publicitario con S)
A PR ____. (Pesadilla con N)
A spin ____. (Asesor de imagen/medios con D)
Take a ____. (Caída en picada con N)
